newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, China shipping firms to discuss links.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, China shipping firms to discuss links.

text.p: Shipping executives from Taiwan and China will meet in Hong Kong in early November for talks on direct links between the island and the mainland, a local newspaper said on Sunday.

The sides were also expected to discuss the status of shipping talks between Taiwan and Hong Kong after the British colony's mid-1997 handover to Chinese sovereignty, the Central Daily News, owned by the ruling Nationalist Party, reported.

The meeting, originally scheduled for this month but postponed for reasons which were not made public, would be held by private organisations representing shipping companies in Taipei and Beijing, it said.
But Taiwan officials told the paper the government would not send any representatives to the meeting and any agreements reached would be subject to government review.
Taiwan in 1995 proposed setting up an offshore trans-shipment centre at southern Kaohsiung port from which ships would be allowed to sail directly between Taiwan and China.
The project has been delayed by sovereignty issues.

On August 20, China unveiled rules governing direct shipping links across the Taiwan strait, effective immediately, but Taiwan responded coolly, saying Beijing's rules were "mingled with sensitive political issues".
Taiwan has banned direct air and shipping links with China since Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists lost the civil war to the Chinese communists and fled to the island in 1949.
Civilian aircraft and vessels have skirted the ban by stopping over in a third country or territory such as the British colony of Hong Kong or Portuguese-run Macau.
